messages:
incident-bot: 514 Pager: Significant throughput degradation detected for eu-inference-prod (metric=token_rate, region=eu). Token/sec down ~55% vs baseline. Alerts: eu-model-exec-low-throughput. Please acknowledge. Link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/2412350001

jon: ack — i'm oncall. grabbing logs and checking model-exec pool health.

priya: i'm joining. seeing errors in model-exec logs related to OOM kicks and long GC pauses on a subset of instances. also noticing a surge in large-batch requests (seq_len>1024) from a customer experiment.

anil: quick check cmds:
```
# sample token rate and pod CPU
curl -s 'https://metrics.redwood/api/v1/query?query=token_rate%7Bregion%3D%22eu%22%7D'
kubectl -n eu get pods -l app=model-exec -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[*].ready}{"\n"}{end}'
```

kate: note — there was a perf test rollout earlier that increased max_seq for certain clients (PR 6890). that could explain the sudden large batches.

priya: root cause hypothesis: combined effect of increased large-batch traffic + a recent runtime mem-change (GC tuning 2025-11-02) -> some model-exec nodes thrashing and dropping throughput, causing backpressure up the stack.

jon: mitigation plan (immediate):
1) circuit-break large request sizes > 1200 tokens for non-SLA routes (temporary).
2) scale up model-exec pod count by +50% and increase pod memory request on new pods to reduce OOMs.
3) enable a temporary per-customer rate cap for the heavy customer identified (customer: VectorLabs).
4) flip on fallback to quantized-medium-v2 for non-critical traffic to reduce memory/CPU pressure.

anil: applying size-circuit now. patch: 
```yaml
# limit-large-seq.yaml
apiVersion: networking.redwood/v1
kind: RateLimit
metadata:
  name: limit-large-seq
spec:
  match:
    - request: {max_sequence_length: 1200}
  action:
    drop: true
```
kubectl apply -f limit-large-seq.yaml
```

ops-automation: circuit rule applied across eu-router in 3s.

priya: scaling model-exec pool now. increasing deployment replicas from 30 -> 45. new nodes requested in the cluster; ETA ~4 minutes to schedule. also adjusting pod memory requests for new replicas.

incident-bot: Incident ticket INC-2412350001 created. Priority: P2.

jon: also enabling fallback routing to quantized-medium-v2 for all non-SLA traffic. this should cut memory/compute per request by ~30%. enabling now.

support-bot: preparing customer advisory template. draft below for review: 

"Customer advisory (short):
Hello — were investigating an ongoing throughput degradation affecting EU inference. Some requests may take longer or be rate-limited temporarily. Our engineers are applying mitigations (scaling execution pool, limiting very large requests, and routing some traffic to a lower-memory quantized model). We expect improvement within ~10 minutes. If you see prolonged impact please reply and we'll prioritize.

If you want to opt out of temporary routing/fallback, contact support and we'll whitelist your calls."

kate: tagging product and infra: the PR that allowed higher seq limits should maybe have gated checks. adding follow-up.

anil: model-exec pods are starting; new pods are Ready=false initially, but scheduling progressing.

priya: 3 minutes after scale start  token_rate up ~20% but still below baseline. GC pause metric improving on new pods.

jon: setting temporary per-customer rate cap for VectorLabs (10 RPS). applied via customer-rate-limiter.

ops-automation: rate cap applied to customer VectorLabs in 2s.

priya: 8 minutes after mitigation: token_rate back to ~85% baseline. CPU and memory pressure dropping. fallback to quantized-medium-v2 handling ~18% of traffic.

kate: support-lead here  sending customer advisory to top 8 affected EU customers now. using support-bot draft.

jon: recommendation for short status page update: 
"Status: Partial degraded throughput in EU - Mitigations underway. Impact: Some requests in EU may experience reduced throughput or temporary rate limiting. Mitigation: scaling model-exec pool, limiting very large requests, and routing a portion of traffic to a quantized variant. ETA: 10-15 minutes for full recovery. Next update: in 15 minutes or on significant change."

priya: note — we should not mention VectorLabs by name on public status page. internal notes only.

jon: agreed. customer-specific actions to be communicated via support only.

anil: 12 minutes after mitigation  token_rate recovered to ~98% baseline. OOM events stopped.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2412350001 status changed to MITIGATED.

jon: proposing follow-ups:
- infra to review cluster autoscaler and pod memory defaults (assignee: anil).
- eng-ml to add pre-warm or staged rollout for large-sequence model parameters (assignee: priya, ticket ENG-7904).
- product to add gating for seq-limit increases and a rollout checklist (assignee: kate).

priya: also recommend adding a runtime metric alert for sustained large-batch ratio > 10% to warn earlier.

anil: opening infra ticket INC-FW-241235 for autoscaler tuning.

support-bot: customer messages sent to affected customers. no inbound escalations yet.

jon: handing off monitoring to kate at 04:10 UTC — summary: circuit-break applied for large seq, model-exec pool scaled +50%, fallback routing enabled for non-SLA traffic, per-customer rate cap applied for heavy client.

kate: ack. I'll keep monitoring dashboards and post any regressions here. scheduling a 30-min post-incident sync today for RCA.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2412350001 status changed to RESOLVED. Resolution summary: throughput drop caused by sudden increase in large-batch requests combined with runtime memory/GC behavior; mitigations included circuit-breaking oversized requests, scaling model-exec pool, routing fallback to quantized model, and temporary per-customer rate limits. Follow-ups assigned.

jon: final note: please include a short internal customer-facing RCA template for support to use in follow-up emails. I'll draft and post in the incident channel in 45 minutes. great job everyone. :thumbsup:
